key_insights.summary: The sparse peer exchange topology achieves full coverage (mean_final_coverage=0.5625, but full_coverage_wrong_answer_rate=1.0) meaning all agents eventually have an answer but it is incorrect. This indicates that the sink merge operation (llm_full_merge) is not correcting errors; instead it may be propagating a wrong consensus.
key_insights.title: Full coverage with zero accuracy: sink merge failure

operation_recommendations.instruction: Reduce the number of peer exchanges per agent (e.g., from 2 to 1) to lower message cost without sacrificing coverage gain, since gain per message is low.

recommended_actions: Limit each agent to at most one peer exchange.
Use a fan-in of 2 instead of 3 to reduce redundant messages.
key_insights.summary: Mean coverage gain is only 0.4375, meaning that after initial local solves, the peer exchange only adds about 44% new coverage. With 20 messages and 25 model calls per run, the communication is inefficient: many messages do not expand coverage.
key_insights.title: Low coverage gain despite high message count
